clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old female presented with multiple, itchy, pearly papules and erythematous nodules on her scalp of 6 months duration, with ulcerations and bleeding after scratching. A skin biopsy was performed, which revealed histopathological features consistent with Angiolymphoid Hyperplasia with Eosinophilia (ALHE), including proliferation of variable-sized blood vessels lined by plump histiocytoid endothelial cells and inflammatory infiltrates of lymphocytes and eosinophils in the dermis. The biopsy also showed evidence of Demodex mite infestation in the sebaceous ducts, confirming scalp demodicosis. Based on these clinical and histopathological findings, the diagnosis of ALHE and scalp demodicosis was made.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with multiple, itchy, pearly papules on her scalp of approximately 6 months duration, with ulcerations and discrete bleeding after scratching.
Clinical examination showed multiple, grouped, erythematous papules and nodules on the left temporo-occipital region.

Histopathological examination revealed proliferation of variable-sized blood vessels lined by plump histiocytoid endothelial cells, as well as inflammatory infiltrates comprising lymphocytes and eosinophils in the dermis, supporting ALHE.
Histopathological examination also revealed evidence of Demodex mite infestation in the sebaceous ducts, supporting scalp demodicosis.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Patient denied any history of systemic symptoms or local trauma; systemic examination was unremarkable without regional or systemic lymphadenopathy.
